reason: Refuted on value and on test design. (1) NOT NEW: the next step for IDEAS I-113 already reads 'After 29 Sep: first test whether the peakless 6bba misses are separable (crowding vs dim)' (curation 11, from the r11d-5 skeptic). r12p-6 only puts numbers on that line. (2) THE CAUSE HAS LARGELY BEEN MEASURED, AND IT IS NEITHER MERGED NOR DIM. The v2 exp39 miss study (research/wf_ideas_v2/r1_hyp_detection.notes.md) found: close GT pairs < 7 um 1% ('not a merge problem'); the same local density median as the controls; GT point below 1.2x background 22% vs 20% in the controls (not dim); nearest raw peak median 8.65 um, ~58% at 7-10 um. Its valley test found an intensity valley between the GT point and the peak for only 4% of 326 misses at 7-10 um, so both sit on ONE bright object. Offsets are 42% z-dominant and persist along a track (dz sign agrees with the predecessor 82%). On x138, round 7 (F-TRN-29) found merges with an annotated neighbour 4.6%, z-dominant 41% vs 25-28% in the control, and a z-split ceiling of 1 node. So the leading cause is localisation / off-centre annotation on elongated nuclei. D0's hypothesis space leaves it out. 'Peakless within 5 um' (31% vs 70%) is exactly what a GT point 7-10 um from its object's peak produces, so it is not evidence of crowding. (3) THE PRE-REGISTERED READ IS CONFOUNDED. (a) The DIM rule uses peak prominence, but 69% of misses have no local max within 5 um, so their prominence is ~0 or undefined and '>= 50% below the control p10' is almost foregone. (b) MERGED and DIM are not mutually exclusive, and no rule says which wins. (c) Thresholded-component volume and elongation fire on single z-elongated nuclei (anisotropic PSF, the z-dominant offset class) and on dense or low-threshold tissue. MERGED can therefore fire without any merge and send ~20 GPU-h to a de-merge target. (d) The 2-peak DoG score repeats the valley test (4%), so its answer is predictable. (e) NEITHER kills recall and moves the GPU to I-110, while the existing evidence points to learned localisation (coordhead-v2 / I-261, agenda #7). (f) The MERGED branch's D1, a 'higher-resolution heatmap = XY ds 4x = 1.625 um/voxel', is x138's CURRENT grid (F-MOD-01; the heatmap is (1,4,4) = 1.625 um isotropic), so it is mis-specified. (4) VALUE FOR THE COMPETITION = 0. It is post-deadline, R9 bars retraining, and it changes no kernel or final. The pool it serves caps at +0.029 lab, sits mostly in 6bba, and has an unproven transfer to the private embryos. (5) FEASIBILITY is trivially fine (CPU analysis, byte-identical, touches nothing), but it should not take pre-deadline time.
fix: Do not script it before 29 Sep. After the deadline, replace D0 with a 3-way test whose classes are EXCLUSIVE and include localisation. Rerun the existing v2 valley/offset scripts (valley.py, miss_off.py) on x138's exp60 6bba run-misses (the 595 misses of r11d-1). Pre-registered classes, checked in this order: OFFSET = a final or raw peak at 5-10 um on the same object (no valley), with GT intensity >= control p25. MERGED = a valley or a second DoG peak at >= 4 um from that peak AND GT-scale component volume > 1.6x, measured with an anisotropy-corrected (physical-um) elongation and density-matched controls (same frame, same neighbour count within 12 um). DIM = GT intensity < control p10 (raw intensity, not prominence). ABSENT = none of these. Route by class: OFFSET -> coordhead-v2 / I-261 (paired retrain, G0); MERGED -> a finer heatmap (XY ds 2x = 0.81 um, not 4x) or a neighbourhood-softmax peak loss; DIM -> nnPU (I-113). Curator: add one line to I-113 saying the separability test must include the localisation class (v2 valley 4%, F-TRN-29), and fix the '1.625 um = higher resolution' wording.
realistic_gain: 0 on the finals and the private LB (post-deadline; analysis only). After the deadline its value is a routing decision for a ~20 GPU-h detector program with EV ~+0.002 lab. As designed it would likely misroute (DIM near-automatic, MERGED confounded by elongation), so it adds little over the existing evidence, which already points to localisation. The corrected 3-way version costs ~2-3 CPU eng-h, reuses existing scripts, and is worth running first after 29 Sep.
